previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic epigastric abdominal pain, attributed to gastroparesis and chronic pancreatitis, along with severe hyperglycemia (glucose 615) without ketoacidosis. Pain was managed with oral hydromorphone per her narcotic contract, and insulin therapy was adjusted from 50 to 60 units of Lantus nightly due to improved oral intake and fluctuating glucose levels. She developed urinary retention likely due to narcotics and sedatives, requiring intermittent catheterization; however, she regained spontaneous voiding and did not require a Foley at discharge. A domestic violence concern was addressed, with plans for a restraining order and social support. She remained on her baseline psychiatric and gastrointestinal medications, with no major complications. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged with her primary care provider and urology.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ y/o female with a history of Type 1 Diabetes 
and chronic abdominal pain who presented with a four days 
history of vomiting and diarrhea, elevated blood sugars, 
resolved with within twelve hours of presentation, and patient 
was discharged to followup in two days with primary care 
physician who knows her well.

# Mild Diabetic Ketoacidosis:
Patient was given IV insulin in the ED after which anion gap 
resolved prior to transfer to floor.  Urine sample was obtained 
several hours after initial IV insulin treatment, at which time, 
no ketones were present.  She had no signs of systemic 
infection, and hyperglycemia was felt to be secondary to 
medication non-compliance.  As above, patient has not been on 
insulin pump in recent years, despite stating that she uses one 
at home.  She is not felt to be a safe candidate for insulin 
pump, though she continues to request one, preferring not to 
stick herself with injections multiple times per day.  Patient 
was restarted on home dose of insulin glargine 60 units at 
bedtime with conservative insulin Humalog sliding scale, on 
which her sugars were still elevated to 300s but anion gap was 
closed.  Patient tolerated po ice cream and crackers without 
difficulty and noted resolution of symptoms.  She requested to 
leave against medical advice.  After communicating with PCP and 
___ provider, patient was felt to be safe for discharge with 
PCP followup appointment in two days.  Patient was discharged on 
same insulin regimen and communicated understanding of how to 
dose her insulin.  She states that she uses the conservative 
Humalog insulin sliding scale starting with blood sugar 150, 
similar to prior hospitalization, rather than the one give to 
her by ___ provider in ___.  

# Nausea, Diarrhea, Abdominal Pain:
Patient has history of gastroparesis, chronic narcotics use, 
question of chronic pancreatitis, peptic ulcer disease, and 
frequent readmissions with abdominal pain.  Abdominal exam on 
admission was benign, and patient appeared comfortable. Pain may 
be multifactorial, though it may very likely be secondary to the 
diabetic ketoacidosis, as it resolved by the time of discharge 
with improved blood sugars.  Alternatively, she may have had a 
viral gastroenteritis that was resolving on admission, causing 
her to feel ill and to stop her insulin.  She was continued on 
her home regimen of hydromorphone 2mg po Q3H:PRN, per Dr. 
___ ""ED and Inpatient Care Plan"" protocol, dated ___ 
without any uptitration of medications.  She was also continued 
on home dose omeprazole 40mg daily.  Patient requested to leave 
hospital upon resolution of symptoms.

# Psychosocial Issues
Patient has very complicated social history and multiple 
readmissions, currently being followed weekly by PCP ___ 
___ for close monitoring. Inpatient protocol was followed, as 
recommended in by Dr. ___ in ""ED and Inpatient Care Plan"" 
(dated ___, in OMR) with regards to avoiding narcotics 
contract and avoidance of IV medications, as above. Patient did 
request to leave against medical advice on day of admission. 
Attempt was made to contact Guardian.  Psychiatric liaison 
___, who knows patient well from frequent inpatient 
admissions for several years, was contacted to help communicate 
more effectively with patient.  As above, primary team felt she 
was safe for discharge after direct communication with PCP with 
whom patient had close followup already scheduled.  Patient was 
pleasant upon discharge and became apologetic for her earlier 
behavior.

able to draw blood well; t-pa was not successful
